Template Syntax: Vue uses an HTML-based template syntax that binds the DOM to component instance data using directives like v-bind, v-if, and v-for. Templates are compiled into optimized render functions.
Reactivity: Vue's reactivity system tracks dependencies and automatically updates the DOM when data changes. It uses Proxy objects in Vue 3 to intercept property access and mutations.
Instance: Every Vue component is backed by a component instance holding data, computed properties, methods, and lifecycle hooks. A root instance is created via createApp to mount the application.

Props: Props are custom attributes registered on a component that allow parent-to-child data flow. Vue validates prop types at runtime in development mode to catch bugs early.
Slots: Slots allow parents to inject content into a child component's layout, enabling flexible composition. Named slots and scoped slots provide even more control over content distribution.
Emits: Emits define custom events a component can fire to communicate upward to its parent. Using defineEmits with TypeScript gives type safety for event payloads.
const emit = defineEmits<{ (e: 'submit', id: number): void }>()

ref: ref creates a reactive reference to any value, wrapping it in an object with a .value property. Accessing .value triggers dependency tracking for Vue's reactivity system.
reactive: reactive returns a deeply reactive proxy of an object, working directly with property access without .value. It's best suited for plain objects or arrays with nested data.

const state = reactive({ user: { name: 'Alice' } });
state.user.name = 'Bob';
computed: computed creates derived state that updates automatically when its dependencies change. Computed values are lazily evaluated and cached until their reactive sources change.
watch: watch observes one or more reactive sources and calls a callback when values change, providing old and new values. Use watchEffect for running side effects automatically.

Vue Router: Vue Router is the official routing library for Vue, enabling SPA navigation with nested routes, dynamic segments, and route-level code splitting. It integrates deeply with Vue's reactivity.
Navigation Guards: Navigation guards protect routes from unauthorized access, handle async data fetching before navigation, or cancel navigation conditionally. They can be global, per-route, or in-component.

Pinia: Pinia is the recommended state management library for Vue 3 with a modular architecture, full TypeScript support, and a simple API similar to Composition API. Each store is an object with state, getters, and actions.
State Management: Vue's state management pattern involves lifting shared state into centralized stores, avoiding prop drilling across deeply nested components. Stores are singleton modules accessible from anywhere.
Persistence: State persistence saves store data to localStorage or sessionStorage so it survives page reloads. Plugins like pinia-plugin-persistedstate automate serialization and hydration.

v-model: v-model provides two-way data binding on form inputs, select elements, and textareas. Vue 3's v-model can bind to multiple values and has customizable modifiers like .lazy and .trim.
Validation: Form validation in Vue can be manual with computed properties or use libraries like VeeValidate and Vuelidate. These provide declarative rules, error messages, and async validation.
Form Libraries: Libraries like FormKit or VeeValidate provide form building, validation, and submission handling with minimal boilerplate. They integrate with any UI component library and handle complex nested forms.

Transitions: Vue's transition system automatically applies CSS classes when elements enter or leave the DOM. It supports JavaScript hooks, custom transition classes, and reusable transition components.
Teleport: Teleport allows rendering a component's template fragment outside its parent DOM hierarchy, useful for modals, tooltips, and toasts that need to break out of overflow containers.
Suspense: Suspense manages async dependencies in the component tree, showing fallback content while nested async components resolve. It works with async setup(), dynamic imports, and async components.

Vitest: Vitest is a blazing-fast unit test framework powered by Vite, compatible with Jest API and offering native ESM support, HMR, and parallel execution out of the box.
Vue Test Utils: Vue Test Utils is the official testing utility library for Vue components, providing mount, shallowMount, and utilities for stubbing, mocking, and asserting component behavior.
Cypress: Cypress provides component testing and E2E testing for Vue apps with an interactive runner, automatic waiting, and network stubbing. It mounts components directly in the browser.

useMouse: Composables are functions that leverage the Composition API to encapsulate reusable stateful logic. A useMouse composable tracks mouse position with reactive coordinates that any component can consume.
useLocalStorage: Composables can wrap browser APIs like localStorage with reactive deserialization. The composable pattern allows sharing state across components without Pinia when the scope is small.
Composable Contracts: Well-designed composables follow predictable naming (useXxx), return a plain object or single ref, accept options via a single reactive object, and provide cleanup via onUnmounted.

Typed Props: defineProps with TypeScript generics provides full type safety for component props. The generic syntax is the recommended approach over the runtime declaration for strict typing.
Typed Emits: defineEmits with TypeScript validates event payloads at compile time. The call signature syntax maps event names to their payload types for complete type coverage.
Typed Refs: Type parameters for ref, reactive, and computed enable strict type checking. Template refs use InstanceType to access the component type for direct method calls.

VueUse: VueUse is a collection of over 200 composable utilities for common patterns like geolocation, clipboard, dark mode, media queries, and fetch with reactive state management.
Vue DevTools: Vue DevTools is a browser extension providing component inspection, state editing, timeline profiling, route visualization, and Pinia store debugging with time-travel capabilities.
VitePress: VitePress is a Vue-powered static site generator for documentation. It uses markdown content with Vue components, automatic search, and a default theme optimized for technical docs.
